name: OpenPort Adaptive Least-Privilege Capability Lease Profile v0.1
summary: Executable reference profile for bounded, short-lived, principal-bound capability leases with monotone child attenuation, current-state revalidation, atomic budget consumption, and privacy-minimized audit evidence.
claimBoundary: This profile validates the OpenPort reference capability-lease contract. It does not disclose or certify private production policy, customer configuration, infrastructure topology, model robustness, or prompt-injection immunity.

checks.description: A lease MUST be compiled by intersecting current static authorization with applicable intent, context, route, and parent-lease bounds; an omitted or broader request MUST NOT expand authority.
evidence: manifest filtered to leased tools and resources
response fields projected to the allowed field set
tool, resource, field, row, amount, and mode violations denied

checks.description: A child lease MUST be no broader than its parent across tools, resources, fields, rows, effect amount, effect mode, calls, cost, and expiry.
evidence: broader child request rejected or narrowed
child expiry no later than parent expiry

checks.description: Every security-relevant use MUST revalidate current principal binding, expiry, revocation, static policy version, and applicable upstream state before an effect is committed.
evidence: cross-key lookup is indistinguishable from a missing lease

checks.description: Call and cost budgets MUST be checked and consumed atomically; validation-only preflight MUST NOT consume budget, and idempotent replay MUST NOT double-spend it.
evidence: sixteen concurrent requests against a one-call lease yield exactly one success
preflight validation leaves the budget unchanged

checks.description: Lease audit evidence MUST be structurally complete while omitting raw task text, private policy expressions, customer data, and internal architecture identifiers.
evidence: dimension counts and stable reason codes
no raw task, policy, credential, or topology material
